Performers
Leopold Mannes (piano), Bronislav Gimpel (violin), Luigi Silva (cello) Documented

The label names The Mannes-⁠Gimpel-⁠Silva Trio and prints Gimpel’s given name as Bronislav; that spelling is retained.

[2] [1]
Work version
Original scoring for violin, cello and piano Documented

The original label identifies the movement and the three instruments. The session’s edition and part materials are not established. Section timings follow the score and the recording’s broad contrasts; there is no bar-level alignment or listening review.

[2] [6]
Recorded
1951 Documented

Jonathan Woolf identifies Clara’s Trio as recorded at the same 1951 sessions as the Beethoven coupling. No precise session date is established. The Archive date field separately describes the LP publication.

[4]
Place
Unknown Unknown

The transfer metadata and consulted reissue review do not establish the recording venue. The US release country is not treated as a session location.

[1] [4]
Label
Decca Gold Label Series Documented

Original 33⅓-rpm LP label, not the Forgotten Records reissue.

[2]
Catalogue
DL 9555 Documented

Internet Archive dates the LP to 1951. A contemporary review independently establishes commercial publication by September 1952; the rights assessment uses that documented upper bound.

[2] [1] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 1, band 3; printed label matrix MG 2301 Documented

The Andante is the third movement listed on side 1 and the third segmented derivative. MG 2301 is the printed side matrix. No individual take or tape number is established.

[2] [3]
Transfer
Internet Archive LP digitisation Documented

The item belongs to the Boston Public Library vinyl collection. No unverified personal mastering credit is inferred from operator accounts.

[1]
Transfer date
2021-07-15 Documented

The ripping_date field is 20210715042255. This is the transfer date; the sleeve and labels were scanned separately in June 2021.

[1]
Processing
Technics SL1200MK5 turntable with Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; segmented VBR MP3 access derivative. Documented

The playback and digitisation chain is stated in the item’s lineage field. Equalisation, pitch correction and noise-reduction settings are not documented.

[1] [3]
Composition rights
Public domain under ordinary life-plus-70 terms; the original score was published in 1847 and Clara Schumann died in 1896. Inferred, not documented

This assessment concerns the historical composition and first edition, not an unidentified modern edition or every jurisdiction.

[7] [9]
Recording rights
Territorial EU public-domain basis: commercial publication on Decca DL 9555 documented by September 1952, before 1963. Documented

The project’s pre-1963 rule relies on expiry of the former 50-year phonogram term before the 2013 extension. Audio Engineering reviews this LP in September 1952. The year 1952 is a conservative publication-by date, distinct from the documented 1951 sessions and the Archive’s 1951 release attribution. US recording status is not established. This is not a Creative Commons licence or worldwide clearance.

[5] [2] [10]

Clara Schumann, Piano Trio in G minor, Op. 17: III. Andante; The Mannes-⁠Gimpel-⁠Silva Trio — Leopold Mannes, piano; Bronislav Gimpel, violin; Luigi Silva, cello. Recorded 1951; Decca DL 9555, published by September 1952; Internet Archive LP transfer. Territorial EU public-domain basis; US recording status not established.

  1. Internet Archive — Decca DL 9555 transfer metadata — Original US Decca LP, catalogue DL 9555, date 1951; ensemble, track list, collection, lineage and ripping_date fields.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  2. Decca DL 9555 — original LP labels — Four-page scan inspected visually, especially side 1 on PDF p. 3: Leopold Mannes, Bronislav Gimpel, Luigi Silva; DL 9555, MG 2301; Andante as the third band. Side 2 identifies the ensemble and Beethoven coupling.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  3. Internet Archive — segmented MP3 derivatives — disc1/01.03. Trio In G Minor, Op 17: 3rd Mov't: Andante.mp3; VBR MP3; duration 339.74 seconds.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  4. Jonathan Woolf — Mannes-⁠Gimpel-⁠Silva Trio reissue review, MusicWeb International, May 2019 — Names the trio members and instruments; identifies the Clara recording with the 1951 Beethoven sessions and original Decca DL 9555. Describes the two original Decca LPs as mono.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  5. Edward Tatnall Canby — Record Revue, Audio Engineering, September 1952 — Printed p. 48 (PDF p. 50), under “Some novel Romantics”: Clara Schumann, Trio in G minor, Op. 17; Beethoven, Trio No. 8 in B flat; Mannes-⁠Gimpel-⁠Silva Trio; Decca DL 9555. A contemporary commercial-release review, establishing publication before 1963.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  6. Clara Schumann — Piano Trio, first edition, Breitkopf & Härtel, plate 7562 — Sibley Music Library scan, printed pp. 20–⁠23 inspected visually: piano alone, violin with pizzicato cello, cello continuation, più animato at bar 25, Tempo I and cello melody at bar 53, final G-major cadence.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  7. IMSLP — Piano Trio in G minor, Op. 17 — Composition 1846; first edition, plate 7562, dated 1847 by Hofmeister reference; four movements and original instrumentation.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  8. Los Angeles Philharmonic — Clara Schumann, Piano Trio — Andante characterised as an instrumental song in G major with an E-minor contrasting middle section.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  9. Robert Greenberg — Robert and Clara Schumann Complete Piano Trios, National Recording Registry essay — Pp. 3–⁠4: Clara’s dates, composition of the Trio between May and September 1846, first chamber composition, and previous study and performance of Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven. The essay concerns the later Beaux Arts recording, not this Decca session.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  10. Directive 2011/77/EU — phonogram term and transition — Recitals 1–⁠3 and Article 1(2)–(3): former 50-year term, lawful publication and extension for recordings still protected on 1 November 2013.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
